activities.anchor: Picture the first hour of a mason's working day
activities.caption: call the weight the wall hands you
activities.name: masBlockEstimate

config.prompt: A working week means thousands of bends, lifts and placements. Roughly how much does one concrete block weigh?
config.why: About 20 kg — a brick is 3–4 kg and a mason places hundreds of those, so the handling system (waist-height staging, legs, rotation) is the profession's predictable difference.
config.context: Pallets of brick and block arrive by the tonne and travel up to scaffolds — which is why the scaffold is the trade's most safety-critical structure.

activities.caption: pair each trowel with its job
activities.name: masTrowelMatch

config.prompt: The trowel family — pair each variant with its work:

pairs.right: picks up, carries and spreads mortar — buttering a brick one-handed is the trade's signature motion

config.why: Mortar is alkaline and etches steel — trowels are cleaned and oiled, and a badly maintained one shows in every joint it makes.

activities.anchor: this is weatherproofing disguised as decoration
activities.caption: place the profile on the drainage scale
activities.name: masJointPlace

config.prompt: Joint profiles are drainage decisions. Place a weather-struck joint on the scale:
config.why: A weather-struck joint sheds water downward and outward; a raked joint, however handsome, leaves a ledge that holds it — in freeze–thaw climates that becomes cracked faces and spalled brick within a few winters.

activities.anchor: guarantees consistent coursing without re-measuring every bed
activities.caption: call the course height the pole is marked at
activities.name: masCourseEstimate

config.prompt: One brick plus one bed joint gives the course height. For a 65 mm brick with a 10 mm joint, how tall is one course?
config.why: 75 mm per course — the story pole is marked off in those increments, and an error at course one compounds to the top, where it collides with openings, lintels and ceiling lines that cannot move.

activities.anchor: Code takes the saw seriously as machinery
activities.caption: true or false — the machinery rules
activities.name: masMachinesJudge

statements.s: A masonry saw must be guarded with a semicircular enclosure over the blade.
statements.why: Designed so blade fragments cannot escape if a wheel shatters.

statements.s: The hazard of working on a mixer or pump is the machine running.
statements.why: It is the machine starting — energy sources are locked out and tagged "Do Not Start" before anyone works on one.

statements.s: Diamond-blade saws make the clean cuts that openings demand.
statements.why: Handheld or table-mounted, they are the shaping end of the kit, with grinders chasing and dressing.

statements.s: Hods, mortar boards and wheelbarrows belong to the mixing-and-moving family.
statements.why: The family that mortars the trade together — including the scaffold's material hoists that move tonnes of units.

activities.caption: rebuild the handling system that prevents the toll
activities.name: masHandlingOrder

config.prompt: Rebuild the handling discipline that stops the chronic-injury engine:
items: Stage materials at waist height on scaffolds and boards — no stooping to a ground pallet
Lift with legs and keep the load close to the body
Use half-blocks and split handling where possible
Keep the work at the body's centreline
Rotate tasks so the same joints do not do everything
config.why: The efficient mason and the safe mason are the same person: the wall goes up faster when materials are staged at waist height.

activities.caption: fill the ladder's rungs for silica
activities.name: masSilicaCloze

config.text: For silica the ladder means wet cutting — water at the blade, an engineering control — or vacuum extraction with rated filters; %%0%% where those controls leave exposure above the permissible limit (a time-weighted average of %%1%% micrograms per cubic metre).
config.hint: The last rung protects one person, only if worn and fitted — and the limit is a round number of micrograms.

activities.anchor: It seems obvious: more strength, more durability
activities.caption: find the line the movement refutes
activities.name: masMortarSpot

config.prompt: One line of this mortar spec is wrong — click it:
lines: Walls move — thermal expansion, settlement, moisture.
Mortar's job includes absorbing the movement the wall cannot avoid.
Specify the strongest mortar and the wall will last longest.
A mortar stronger than the units pushes every crack into the bricks themselves.
The mortar is the designed weak link — joints rake out and repoint far more cheaply than units replace.
config.correction: The mortar should be weaker than the units — the soft joint takes the movement and is repaired cheaply; the hard mortar cracks expensive, unrepointable brick.
config.why: The units carry the building, but the mortar carries the wall's life.
